validity.recommendation: Row is real: this is GEM's tracking of the historical direct Altai/western route of the Russia-China gas pipeline project (Tomsk Oblast through Altai Krai to Xinjiang), well documented in Russian and English press/reference sources across 2006-2019. Not a phantom entry.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed. en.wikipedia.org's 'Altai gas pipeline' article and Kommersant (kommersant.ru/doc/4180411, Dec 2019) both describe the same real project: a proposed Gazprom natural-gas trunk from West Siberian gas fields through Tomsk Oblast/Altai Krai (passing Volodino, Novosibirsk, Barnaul, Biysk, the Kanas mountain pass) into Xinjiang, China, to tie into China's West-East Gas Pipeline, first proposed ~2006, with 30 bcm/y design capacity and TomskTransGaz named as the intended Russian-side builder/operator. GEM's row name ('Prokopyevsky-Toutunhe Pipeline') labels it by presumed endpoint place names rather than the common 'Altai gas pipeline' name used everywhere in sources -- confirmed as the same project via route/corridor identity, not literal name match (both url_verifier --name checks failed on this basis; manually overridden, see Fuel/Status fill notes).

validity.researcher_notes: This project (the direct Tomsk-Altai-Xinjiang 'western route') is historically the SAME underlying western-route concept that, per en.wikipedia.org's own 2021-2025 timeline entries, was later revived under a DIFFERENT alignment routed through Mongolia -- which GEM tracks (per this batch's scope guidance) as P0734/Power of Siberia 2. The two are related but were NOT found to be geographically identical in the sources read this leg: this row's route (per en.wikipedia.org) runs Tomsk Oblast -> Novosibirsk -> Barnaul -> Biysk -> Kanas Pass -> Xinjiang directly, whereas the Mongolia-routed PoS-2 alignment (per the same article's later sections, not read in full detail this leg) diverts south through Mongolia before entering China further east. Both share 'western route of the Russia-China gas system' branding in press coverage, which is a plausible source of confusion/potential duplication in how GEM tracks the concept's history across two rows. Recommend whoever next works P0734 cross-check this row's ShelvedYear/CancelledYear/history against P0734's ProposalYear and any 'formerly known as Altai pipeline' notes, to confirm GEM is not double-counting one project's history as two separate pipeline entities. Not resolved this leg -- P0734 is out of the R6 Siberia roster.

Summary: en.wikipedia.org's timeline has 2013 (Gazprom/CNPC prioritize the eastern Power-of-Siberia route instead), 2014 (western-route talks 'resumed'), and 2015 ('postponed for an indefinite period of time') -- none of which lines up cleanly with a 2014 shelving date, and 2014 in particular reads as a resumption rather than a pause in Wikipedia's own framing. No source found this leg states a 2016 cancellation event. This is a candidate case for ShelvedCancelledType=inferred (dormancy-based inference from 'no positive developments on this specific alignment since 2015/2019') rather than a sourced, dated formal cancellation -- flagging for a future pass to verify against whatever source(s) originally supported the 2014/2016 years, which were not identified this leg.

fills.researcher_notes: Status='cancelled' is directionally supported but the wording is softer in both sources than a clean 'cancelled': en.wikipedia.org states the project was 'postponed for an indefinite period of time' in 2015, after Gazprom/CNPC chose the eastern Power of Siberia route in 2013-2014; Kommersant (Dec 2019) still frames it as Russia 'may temporarily abandon' the western route (может временно отказаться) — softer than a final cancellation, and notably Kommersant's own headline explains WHY: Xinjiang's own domestic gas production had grown enough that the original commercial rationale (feeding gas-poor Xinjiang) was undercut, which is a durable/structural reason rather than a temporary funding pause. Neither source uses the word 'cancelled'; both instead use shelved/postponed-indefinitely language, and no source (in this lean-pass budget) was found describing a formal cancellation announcement. All positive project developments 2021-2025 (per the wikipedia timeline) are specifically about a DIFFERENT alignment (the Mongolia-routed Power of Siberia 2 western pipeline, i.e. this batch's out-of-roster P0734), not a revival of this Tomsk-Barnaul-Xinjiang direct alignment. On balance: REFS_ADDED at medium tier (not high) because the sources corroborate the project is dead/inactive but describe it with 'shelved/postponed-indefinitely' language rather than literally 'cancelled' — filed a spec concern in validity[] recommending GEM re-examine Status vs the ShelvedCancelledType vocabulary distinction for this row, and flagging that neither the recorded ShelvedYear=2014 nor CancelledYear=2016 is corroborated by any source found (see Shelved/Cancelled fills, both UNRESOLVED).

Could not corroborate ShelvedYear=2014 — the two independent sources available this leg actually put the relevant milestones in different years, and 2014 reads as the OPPOSITE of a shelving in en.wikipedia.org's own timeline: 2013 is when Gazprom/CNPC agreed to prioritize the eastern route (Power of Siberia) over this western/Altai route; 2014 is described as a 'resumption' of the western-route talks (APEC-summit-adjacent); 2015 is when the project was 'postponed for an indefinite period of time' — the year that most resembles GEM's own 'shelved' concept. Kommersant (Dec 2019) gives no specific shelving year at all, framing the western route as still-notionally-alive-but-likely-to-be-abandoned as late as end of 2019. Searched (lean-pass budget: one targeted second-source check) but found no primary source pinning a 2014 shelving date specifically; not staging a corrected value either, since 2015 (the best candidate from Wikipedia alone) is not independently corroborated by a second source within this leg's budget. Flagged as a spec concern in validity[] rather than silently leaving the year uncorroborated with no trace — recommend a future pass re-examine ShelvedYear against Wikipedia's cited primary sources (not reached this pass) or Russian-language 2014-2015 press specifically dated to the postponement announcement.

Could not corroborate CancelledYear=2016. Neither source available this leg mentions a 2016 event for this project at all: en.wikipedia.org's timeline jumps from '2015 postponed indefinitely' straight to 2021-2025 developments, all of which concern the DIFFERENT Mongolia-routed alignment (out-of-roster P0734/Power of Siberia 2), not this Tomsk-Altai-Xinjiang direct alignment; Kommersant (Dec 2019) treats the western route as still an open, not-yet-finalized question at that date, which is itself hard to square with a formal 2016 cancellation (a source three years later would not still describe a live decision if it had already been formally cancelled). Searched within lean-pass budget; found nothing pinning 2016 specifically. Also relevant to ShelvedCancelledType: since no source states a formal cancellation announcement (only 'postponed indefinitely' language), if GEM's own convention is that a project inferred-dead from prolonged inactivity should carry ShelvedCancelledType=inferred (lowercase) rather than confirmed, that determination is out of this leg's scope to change but is flagged in the spec concern in validity[] for whoever next touches ShelvedCancelledType on this row.

General route/corridor corroborated (REFS_ADDED-quality) but the two specific place names GEM records are NOT found verbatim in either source, so staging as UNRESOLVED rather than a false-precision REFS_ADDED. en.wikipedia.org's route list (infobox) reads: Alexandrovskoye, Vertikos, Parabel, Chazhemto, Volodino, Boyarka, Novosibirsk, Barnaul, Biysk, the Kanas mountain pass -> Xinjiang region (West-East Gas Pipeline), China — i.e. Russia (Tomsk Oblast/Altai Krai) to China (Xinjiang) generally matches StartCountryOrArea=Russia / EndCountryOrArea=Russia->China / EndState/Province=Xinjiang, but neither 'Prokopyevsky District' (Kemerovo Oblast, not listed among the named waypoints) nor 'Toutunhe' (a district of Urumqi, Xinjiang -- plausible as the specific West-East Gas Pipeline tie-in point but not named in the source) appears in either source read this leg. Recommend ShelvedCancelledType be reviewed for 'inferred' (lowercase) given no source states a formal cancellation announcement -- see spec concern in validity[]. Not changing status; not marking stale, since the underlying conclusion (long-dormant, dead) is well within the dormancy rule regardless of exact evidence date.
